months.name: January
months.note: Drop the high Sierra, Rockies, and Cascades. The winter belt is the low desert: Imperial, Blythe, Quartzsite, Yuma.

months.name: February
months.note: Still winter-belt season. High country stays snowed in.

months.name: March
months.note: Desert is still the easy month. Watch wind. Sierra passes are not a trailer plan.

months.name: April
months.note: LTVA fee season ends April 15. After that, 14-day rules apply where camping is still open. Desert starts to warm.

months.name: May
months.note: Low desert is already hot by late May. Move up in elevation if you are still out there.

months.name: June
months.note: Low desert is a bad month. Mountains and the Northwest are the point.

months.name: July
months.note: Desert heat warning. Afternoon temperatures in Imperial, Blythe, Quartzsite, and Yuma are dangerous. This is not a cheap summer home.

months.name: August
months.note: Same heat, plus monsoon storms and flash floods in desert washes.

months.name: September
months.note: LTVA fee season starts September 15. Early September is still hot. Do not treat the permit as free camping.

months.name: October
months.note: First comfortable desert month. High country is still open early, then starts to close.

months.name: November
months.note: Winter belt is honest again. High Sierra and the Rockies are a gamble.

months.name: December
months.note: Short days, cold nights, snow in the high country. Desert LTVAs are the seasonal public-land option, and they are a permit.
